scope: Local macOS arm64 signed WSS, Store, actual Core/RTC G.711 audio; isolated synthetic fixtures and default stacks. No model-host/account/provider invocation or publication. Component Core harness opt0; integration release graph Core opt3 and Connect store/service/server opt0, selected test stripping disabled.
implementation: Signed connection.update hold/resume/mute/unmute uses the exact original current WSS PeerAdmission, WebRTC Endpoint, runtime Connection/generation and Store stream-command lease. It does not select a native transport adapter or borrow native negotiation authority.

A separate immutable invocation plan retains the exact validated action, actual audio stream IDs and expected revision. Core receives only this held gate intent under current owner authority. Endpoint hold directions map to the reversed server port; inactive hold pauses both directions without reallocating or renegotiating resources.

Original Core gate control waits for the scene metadata slot under its existing credential/control cutoff, cancellation and shutdown. Current authority and exact revision are checked after acquisition and before the one quiescent commit. Genuine conflicts and uncertain outcomes are never automatically retried.

Only returned Core success and its captured logical gate states can produce the original lease gate receipt. Durable metadata recovery retains that receipt, not live command readers or permission to repeat IO. Current completed replay returns the historical original result/effect and cannot reset later gate state.
behavior: Both EdDSA/ES256 new real signed RTC journeys first complete the existing actual marked duplex/subscription/replay/stale/unsubscribe/reselect path.

A same-credential foreign physical WSS peer cannot execute the original gate; the original peer then completes that logical operation with one effect/attempt. A live peer controlling its own RTC connection without connection.update scope is refused, without changing its revision.
Stale revision, unavailable stream and unsupported quality update are explicitly refused while the original decoded duplex and revision stay current.

Source mute suppresses only publication and preserves reverse playback; unmute restores identified decoded duplex. Endpoint recvonly hold suppresses its publication and preserves playback; sendonly preserves publication and suppresses playback. Inactive hold silences both; each resume restores both markers.
Current mute replay while muted and superseded mute replay after resume return the exact original receipt/effect without a new Core revision or restoring old mute state.

Actual transport IDs, stream-local handles, stream/Connection generations, negotiated bindings, opening budgets, two original routes and two total RTC allocations stay unchanged. The final explicit end completes using the later gate revision, joins/releases only the original route, replays its one end effect and leaves WSS control usable.
